newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, China exchange notes on securities markets.
newsitem.headline: Japan, China exchange notes on securities markets.

text.p: Japan and China exchanged notes on Tuesday in Beijing to promote information exchange about securities and securities derivatives markets in the two countries, the Japanese Foreign Ministry said.

The action will pave the way for the listing of shares in Chinese firms on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE), a ministry official said. Japanese and Chinese securities regulators will conclude a memorandum of understanding soon, he said.
TSE president Mitsuhide Yamaguchi welcomed the move, saying the bourse would make further efforts to attract Chinese firms.
Japanese media reports have said two Chinese firms are likely to be listed on the TSE next year following the exchange of notes.
Worried by the delisting of foreign companies from Japanese stock exchanges, the TSE has eased listing requirements to lure companies from the rest of Asia.
In February 1996, Malaysia's YTL Corp Bhd became the first Asian company to list on the TSE.
